newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close down on broad-based selling.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close down on broad-based selling.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Saturday's half-day session on broad-based selling, brokers said.
The composite index shed 3.46 points, or 0.44 percent, to end at 781.73. Declining stocks beat advancers, 521 to 270.

"Selling was broad-based as the overall sentiment remained depressed," said a Daewoo Securities broker. "Only a handful of small-cap stocks posted gains, but they were well overshadowed by blue-chip weakeness."
Samsung Electronics continued to fall, easing 300 won to 56,900. LG Chemical lost 300 won to 10,900.
Commercial Bank of Korea added 20 won to close at 7,220, but brokers saw little direct impact on the stock price from Friday's brisk earnings forecast by a bank official.
An official of the bank told a UBS Securities Investor Forum on Friday that the bank's net profit was expected to rise to 135 billion won this year from 92 billion in 1995.
The index futures December contracts fell 1.50 points to 82.30 while the KOSPI 200 index lost 0.44 points to 82.20.
